```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_scip <- requireNamespace("scip", quietly = TRUE)
has_osqp <- requireNamespace("osqp", quietly = TRUE)
has_nloptr <- requireNamespace("nloptr", quietly = TRUE)
```

```{r setup}
library(optcompR)
```

optcompR describes an optimization problem once, as variables, expressions,
constraints and an objective, and then classifies it, chooses a capable solver
```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = requireNamespace("symcompR", quietly = TRUE))
```

symcompR is a computer algebra system for R. optcompR converts expressions in
both directions, so a model can be derived symbolically and solved
numerically, or a model expression can be simplified and differentiated
symbolically.

## From symcompR to optcompR

Symbols map to variables with the same name (or through `map`).

```{r}
library(symcompR)
m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x")
y <- opt_variable(m, "y")
s <- (Symbol("x") - 1)^2 + Symbol("x") * Symbol("y") + exp(Symbol("y"))
e <- opt_from_sym(m, s)
e
opt_objective(m, e)
opt_classify(m)$class
```

## From optcompR to symcompR

```{r}
m2 <- opt_model()
z <- opt_variable(m2, "z")
f <- 3 * z^2 + exp(z)
sf <- opt_to_sym(f)
sf
diff(sf, Symbol("z"))
```

## Checking derivatives symbolically

The symbolic derivative and optcompR's exact gradient agree:

```{r}
opt_objective(m2, f)
opt_gradient(m2, c(z = 0.7))
6 * 0.7 + exp(0.7)
```

External functions created with `opt_function()` have no symbolic form and
cannot be converted.
